standard.label: Standard
standard.summary: The common reading. A foil unlocks its family the way the community usually plays it, and gathering an item before its card is unlocked is allowed as long as you bank it.
caveats: You may gather and bank an item before its card is unlocked. You just cannot use it until then.

sources.label: Project brief - downward unlocks
osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say
sources.quote: vertical/downward unlocks, described as the leading consensus

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.summary: The strict cardlocked-ironman reading. The same cards are unlocked, but you may not interact with a locked source at all - no gathering ahead of the unlock and no pre-banking.
caveats: Any interaction with a locked source is off the table. You cannot gather, mine, chop or catch a card you have not unlocked, even to bank it.

sources.label: Extreme defined from the osrscardexchange framing only
Extreme's definition drops the unread Reddit thread; osrscardexchange stands alone as its source
osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say

plain-foil.label: Plain foil
plain-foil.summary: A foil is just a shiny duplicate. It unlocks the card it shows and nothing more. A vocal minority position, shown here as a first-class answer rather than an error.
caveats: This is one of three community camps, not a settled rule. It is the most conservative reading available.

sources.label: osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say
sources.quote: a foil is just a foil

rules.explanation: An item with an unprocessed and a processed form unlocks both forms of {card} and nothing else. It does not descend any ladder the card also sits in.
caveats: Not everyone reads it this way. One community source treats a foil fish as unlocking every fish caught the same way. That reading is recorded here as input and not adopted - a pair is one item in two forms, so it stops a descent rather than starting one.
